title: Session Generation Effectiveness — Orchestrator Pipeline Analysis

orchestrator_architecture.pipeline_model: verify live state → generate plan → execute plan → validate outcome
orchestrator_architecture.key_difference: v1 had 4 human decision layers. v2 has 0 — all structural decisions automated by orchestrator.
orchestrator_architecture.plan_generation: buildS852(), buildS853(), buildS854() — each produces a structured JSON session package
orchestrator_architecture.dependency_handling: S852 must precede S853 (manifest must be clean before certification). S854 runs post-execution.
orchestrator_architecture.parallelism: S852 → S853 (can run in parallel with S852 verification) → S854

error_handling.dl029_detection: Detected 351/351 stale manifest entries. Rejected stale data. Generated S852 as prerequisite.
error_handling.dl033_naming: Session package listed P1-ED-* and P1-FD-* items as "pack_c". Execution script used QID-prefix-based pack assignment to correct automatically. All items certified in correct target files.
error_handling.zero_execution_failures: All 3 session packages executed successfully. No retries needed.
error_handling.zero_human_intervention: No manual corrections to orchestrator output.

autonomy_assessment.level: FULL — orchestrator detected stale data, generated prerequisite sessions, planned certification batches, enforced governance constraints, and handled naming edge cases — all without human decision points
human_actions: Plan approval (orchestrator manifest sign-off) — the single governance gate
autonomy_assessment.automation_boundary: Content decisions (which items to certify, what to modify) remain human-approved. Structural decisions (manifest state, batch sizing, dependency ordering, defect detection) are fully automated.

verdict: SESSION_GENERATION_EFFECTIVE — The orchestrator successfully replaced the v1 "analyze → interpret → plan → execute" pipeline (4 human decision layers) with "verify live state → generate plan → execute plan → validate outcome" (0 human decision layers). It handled stale artifact detection (DL-029), dependency ordering (S852→S853→S854), batch-size enforcement (Rule 5), and naming corrections (DL-033) autonomously. The orchestrator is now the backbone of the unattended session model.
